def generate_man(prog):
    date = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    return f""".TH XH 1 {date} {VERSION} "User Commands"

.SH NAME
xh \\- Friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests

.SH SYNOPSIS
.B xh
[\\fIOPTIONS\\fR]
[\\fIMETHOD\\fR]
\\fIURL\\fR
[\\-\\-]
[\\fIREQUEST_ITEM\\fR ...]

.SH DESCRIPTION

\\fBxh\\fR is an HTTP client with a friendly command line interface. It strives to
have readable output and easy-to-use options.

xh is mostly compatible with HTTPie: see \\fBhttp\\fR(1).

The \\fB--curl\\fR option can be used to print a \\fBcurl\\fR(1) translation of the
command instead of sending a request.

.SH POSITIONAL ARGUMENTS
.TP 4
[\\fIMETHOD\\fR]\\fI
The HTTP method to use for the request.

This defaults to GET, or to POST if the request contains a body.
.TP
\\fIURL\\fR
The URL to request.

The URL scheme defaults to "http://" normally, or "https://" if
the program is invoked as "xhs".

A leading colon works as shorthand for localhost. ":8000" is equivalent
to "localhost:8000", and ":/path" is equivalent to "localhost/path".
.TP
[\\fIREQUEST_ITEM\\fR ...]
Optional key\\-value pairs to be included in the request.

The separator is used to determine the type:
.RS 8
.TP 4
key==value
Add a query string to the URL.
.TP 4
key=value
Add a JSON property (\\-\\-json) or form field (\\-\\-form) to the request body.
.TP 4
key:=value
Add a field with a literal JSON value to the request body.

Example: "numbers:=[1,2,3] enabled:=true"
.TP 4
key@filename
Upload a file (requires \\-\\-form or \\-\\-multipart).

To set the filename and mimetype, ";type=" and ";filename=" can be used respectively.

Example: "pfp@ra.jpg;type=image/jpeg;filename=profile.jpg"
.TP 4
@filename
Use a file as the request body.
.TP 4
header:value
Add a header, e.g. "user\\-agent:foobar"
.TP 4
header:
Unset a header, e.g. "connection:"
.TP 4
header;
Add a header with an empty value.
.RE

.RS
An "@" prefix can be used to read a value from a file. For example: "x\\-api\\-key:@api\\-key.txt".

A backslash can be used to escape special characters, e.g. "weird\\\\:key=value".

To construct a complex JSON object, the REQUEST_ITEM's key can be set to a JSON path instead of a field name. For more information on this syntax, refer to https://httpie.io/docs/cli/nested\\-json.
.RE

.SH OPTIONS
Each --OPTION can be reset with a --no-OPTION argument.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-j\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-json\\fR
(default) Serialize data items from the command line as a JSON object.

Overrides both \\-\\-form and \\-\\-multipart.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-f\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-form\\fR
Serialize data items from the command line as form fields.

Overrides both \\-\\-json and \\-\\-multipart.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-multipart\\fR
Like \\-\\-form, but force a multipart/form-data request even without files.

Overrides both \\-\\-json and \\-\\-form.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-raw\\fR=\\fIRAW\\fR
Pass raw request data without extra processing.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-pretty\\fR=\\fISTYLE\\fR
Controls output processing. Possible values are:

    all      (default) Enable both coloring and formatting
    colors   Apply syntax highlighting to output
    format   Pretty\\-print json and sort headers
    none     Disable both coloring and formatting

Defaults to "format" if the NO_COLOR env is set and to "none" if stdout is not tty.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-format\\-options\\fR=\\fIFORMAT_OPTIONS\\fR
Set output formatting options. Supported option are:

    json.indent:<NUM>
    json.format:<true|false>
    headers.sort:<true|false>

Example: \\-\\-format\\-options=json.indent:2,headers.sort:false.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-s\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-style\\fR=\\fITHEME\\fR
Output coloring style.

[possible values: auto, solarized, monokai, fruity]
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-response\\-charset\\fR=\\fIENCODING\\fR
Override the response encoding for terminal display purposes.

Example: \\-\\-response\\-charset=latin1.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-response\\-mime\\fR=\\fIMIME_TYPE\\fR
Override the response mime type for coloring and formatting for the terminal.

Example: \\-\\-response\\-mime=application/json.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-p\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-print\\fR=\\fIFORMAT\\fR
String specifying what the output should contain

    'H' request headers
    'B' request body
    'h' response headers
    'b' response body
    'm' response metadata

Example: \\-\\-print=Hb.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-h\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-headers\\fR
Print only the response headers. Shortcut for \\-\\-print=h.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-b\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-body\\fR
Print only the response body. Shortcut for \\-\\-print=b.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-m\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-meta\\fR
Print only the response metadata. Shortcut for \\-\\-print=m.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-v\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-verbose\\fR
Print the whole request as well as the response.

Additionally, this enables \\-\\-all for printing intermediary requests/responses while following redirects.

Using verbose twice i.e. \\-vv will print the response metadata as well.

Equivalent to \\-\\-print=HhBb \\-\\-all.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-debug\\fR
Print full error stack traces and debug log messages.

Logging can be configured in more detail using the `$RUST_LOG` environment variable. Set
`RUST_LOG=trace` to show even more messages. See
https://docs.rs/env_logger/0.11.3/env_logger/#enabling\\-logging.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-all\\fR
Show any intermediary requests/responses while following redirects with \\-\\-follow
.TP 4
\\fB\\-P\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-history\\-print\\fR=\\fIFORMAT\\fR
The same as \\-\\-print but applies only to intermediary requests/responses
.TP 4
\\fB\\-q\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-quiet\\fR
Do not print to stdout or stderr.

Using quiet twice i.e. \\-qq will suppress warnings as well.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-S\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-stream\\fR
Always stream the response body
.TP 4
\\fB\\-x\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-compress\\fR
Content compressed (encoded) with Deflate algorithm.

The Content\\-Encoding header is set to deflate.

Compression is skipped if it appears that compression ratio is negative. Compression can
be forced by repeating this option.

Note: Compression cannot be used if the Content\\-Encoding request header is present.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-o\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-output\\fR=\\fIFILE\\fR
Save output to FILE instead of stdout
.TP 4
\\fB\\-d\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-download\\fR
Download the body to a file instead of printing it.

The Accept\\-Encoding header is set to identify and any redirects will be followed.
.TP 4
\\fB\\-c\\fR, \\fB\\-\\-continue\\fR
Resume an interrupted download. Requires \\-\\-download and \\-\\-output
.TP 4
\\fB\\-\\-session\\fR=\\fIFILE\\fR
Create, or reuse and update a session.

Within a session, custom headers, auth credentials, as well as any cookies sent by the
server persist between requests.

def build_request_items(opts, positional, stdin_data):

    prog_base = os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])
    is_https_default = False
    if prog_base in ["xhs","https","xhttps"]:
        is_https_default = True
    if opts.https:
        is_https_default = True
    default_scheme = opts.default_scheme if opts.default_scheme else ("https" if is_https_default else "http")

    method = None
    url_tok = None
    items = []
    if not positional:
        missing_url()
    # Check for help already
    if len(positional) >= 2:
        cand = positional[0]
        nxt = positional[1]
        cand_is_url = is_url_token(cand) or "://" in cand or cand.startswith(":")
        nxt_is_url = is_url_token(nxt) or "://" in nxt or nxt.startswith(":")
        cand_has_sep = looks_like_request_item(cand)
        if not cand_is_url and nxt_is_url and not cand_has_sep:
            method = cand.upper()
            url_tok = nxt
            items = positional[2:]
        elif not cand_is_url and cand.upper() in ["GET","POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH","HEAD","OPTIONS","CONNECT","TRACE"] and nxt_is_url:
            method = cand.upper()
            url_tok = nxt
            items = positional[2:]
        elif not cand_is_url and not cand_has_sep and not looks_like_request_item(nxt):
            # FOO BAR case
            method = cand.upper()
            url_tok = nxt
            items = positional[2:]
        else:
            url_tok = cand
            items = positional[1:]
    else:
        url_tok = positional[0]
        items = positional[1:]

    if url_tok and not is_url_token(url_tok) and not "://" in url_tok and not url_tok.startswith(":"):
        if len(positional)==1 and re.match(r'^[A-Za-z]+$', url_tok):
            missing_url2()

    try:
        parsed, url_full = resolve_url(url_tok, default_scheme)
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        xh_error(str(e))

    # Query handling later
    host_header = parsed.netloc

    query_params = []
    json_data = {}
    file_fields = []
    headers_ordered = []
    headers_unset = set()
    headers_empty = set()
    body_file = None
    has_data = False

        if it.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it,0):
            if body_file is not None:
                xh_error("Request body (from a file) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.")
            if opts.raw is not None:
                error_exit(f"error: Request body (from --raw) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.\n\nUsage: xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)
            body_file = it[1:]
            has_data = True
            # check file exists early?
            # For file body, we will later read

    # If body_file set, ensure no other data items that would conflict
    if body_file is not None:
        # Check other items contain = etc that would be data
        for it in items:
            if it.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it,0):
                continue
            # if it is query, that's allowed? But binary said query+data mixing allowed but body file + data not allowed. For query params, they are allowed with body file? Let's allow query.
            idx_q = find_unescaped(it, "==")
            if idx_q != -1:
                continue
            # else any = or := or @ file field should error
            if find_unescaped(it, ":=")!=-1 or find_unescaped(it, "=")!=-1 or find_unescaped(it, "@")!=-1:
                # but need to differentiate file field @ vs query? Already filtered
                if find_unescaped(it, "@")!=-1 and not it.endswith(";") and ":" not in it:
                    # file field
                    xh_error("Request body (from a file) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.")
                elif find_unescaped(it, ":=")!=-1 or find_unescaped(it, "=")!=-1:
                    xh_error("Request body (from a file) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.")
                else:

                    pass

        # proceed to parse only query and headers, not data
        # We'll need to parse remaining items as headers/query only
        # Re-parse for query and headers
        for it in items:
            if it.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it,0):
                continue
            idx_q = find_unescaped(it, "==")
            if idx_q != -1:
                k = unescape(it[:idx_q])
                v = it[idx_q+2:]
                if v.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it, idx_q+2):
                    fpath=v[1:]
                    try:
                        with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                            v=f.read().rstrip('\n')
                    except FileNotFoundError:
                        xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                else:
                    v=unescape(v)
                query_params.append((k,v))
                continue

            idx_colon = find_unescaped(it, ":")
            idx_semi = find_unescaped(it, ";")
            # header with colon
            if idx_colon!=-1:

                v=it[idx_colon+1:]
                if v.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it, idx_colon+1):
                    fpath=v[1:]
                    try:
                        with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                            v=f.read().rstrip('\r\n')
                    except FileNotFoundError:
                        xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                else:
                    v=unescape(v)
                if v=="" and not it.endswith(";"):
                    headers_unset.add(k.lower())
                else:
                    if v=="":
                        headers_unset.add(k.lower())
                    else:
                        headers_ordered.append((k,v))
                continue
            if idx_semi!=-1 and it.endswith(";") and find_unescaped(it,";")==len(it)-1:
                k=unescape(it[:-1])
                headers_empty.add(k.lower())
                headers_ordered.append((k,""))
                continue
            # For body_file case, other items that are not query/header are errors? Already handled data mixing
            # So headers handled, query handled, others would have errored
            # But what about "=" data that already errored? Already xh_error
        return method, parsed, url_full, query_params, json_data, file_fields, headers_ordered, headers_unset, headers_empty, body_file, has_data

    # No body_file, parse all items
    for it in items:
        # query ==
        idx_q = find_unescaped(it, "==")
        if idx_q != -1:
            k = unescape(it[:idx_q])
            v = it[idx_q+2:]
            if v.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it, idx_q+2):
                fpath=v[1:]
                try:
                    with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                        v=f.read().rstrip('\n')
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
            else:
                v=unescape(v)
                # also handle reading? query value may have @ file? Already handled above for starting @
                # But for value with @ not at start, not needed
            query_params.append((k,v))
            continue
        # raw json :=
        idx_colon_eq = find_unescaped(it, ":=")
        if idx_colon_eq != -1:
            k = unescape(it[:idx_colon_eq])
            v_raw = it[idx_colon_eq+2:]
            if v_raw.startswith("@"):
                fpath=v_raw[1:]
                try:
                    with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                        content=f.read()
                        v=json.loads(content)
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
                    xh_error("expected value at line 1 column 1")
            else:
                try:
                    if v_raw=="":
                        xh_error("expected value at line 1 column 1")
                    v=json.loads(v_raw)
                except SystemExit:
                    raise
                except Exception as e:
                    # produce trailing characters error if needed
                    err_str=str(e)
                    # For binary, message includes "trailing characters at line 1 column 4" etc. We'll include err_str
                    error_exit(f"error: Invalid value for '[REQUEST_ITEM]...': \"{it}\" {err_str}\n\nUsage: {PROG} [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)
            if opts.form or opts.multipart:
                error_exit(f"error: Invalid value for '[REQUEST_ITEM]...': \"{it}\" expected value at line 1 column 1\n\nUsage: {PROG} [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)
            try:
                tokens=parse_path(k)
            except SystemExit:
                raise
            deep_set(json_data, tokens, v)
            has_data=True
            continue
        # = case
        idx_eq = find_unescaped(it, "=")
        # But need to check for file field before =? Actually file field uses @ without =. So idx_eq would be -1 for foo@bar. So order: check "=" first, then later "@" for file field.
        if idx_eq != -1:
            k = unescape(it[:idx_eq])
            v_raw = it[idx_eq+1:]
            if v_raw.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it, idx_eq+1):
                fpath=v_raw[1:]
                try:
                    with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                        content=f.read()
                        # For "=" case, content is string including maybe newline? Keep as is, but for json we need to preserve newline? We'll keep exactly.
                        # If file not found, error
                        v=content
                        # Note: json string will be encoded, newline will be \n
                        # For header handling? This is data, not header.
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
                except Exception as e:
                    xh_error(str(e))
            else:
                v=unescape(v_raw)
            if opts.raw is not None:
                error_exit(f"error: Request body (from --raw) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.\n\nUsage: xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)
            try:
                tokens=parse_path(k)
            except SystemExit:
                raise
            deep_set(json_data, tokens, v)
            has_data=True
            continue
        # file field @
        idx_at = find_unescaped(it, "@")
        if idx_at != -1 and not it.startswith("@"):
            if opts.json and not opts.form and not opts.multipart:
                xh_error("Can't use file fields in JSON mode (perhaps you meant --form?)")
            k=unescape(it[:idx_at])
            v_part=it[idx_at+1:]
            parts=v_part.split(";")
            fpath=unescape(parts[0])
            ftype=None
            fname_param=None
            for p in parts[1:]:
                if p.startswith("type="):
                    ftype=p[5:]
                elif p.startswith("filename="):
                    fname_param=p[9:]
            file_fields.append((k,fpath,ftype,fname_param))
            has_data=True
            continue
        # header colon
        idx_colon = find_unescaped(it, ":")
        if idx_colon != -1:
            k=unescape(it[:idx_colon])
            v=it[idx_colon+1:]
            if v.startswith("@") and not is_escaped(it, idx_colon+1):
                fpath=v[1:]
                try:
                    with open(fpath,'r') as f:
                        v=f.read().rstrip('\r\n')
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    xh_error("No such file or directory (os error 2)")
            else:
                v=unescape(v)
            # Header with empty value '' and colon at end => unset
            # For "header;" empty value case, it ends with ";", not ":".
            # So here, if v=="" -> unset
            # But need to differentiate "header:" vs "header: " with space
            # If original it has "header:" and nothing after, then unset
            # If it has "header: " with space, v would be " " after unescape? That would be not empty, so treat as header with space value?
            # In observed, "header:" removed, "header;" gave empty. So we handle.
            if v=="" and not it.endswith(";"):
                headers_unset.add(k.lower())
            else:
                if v=="":
                    headers_unset.add(k.lower())
                else:
                    # Check if headers_unset already contains? Remove?
                    # Also need to handle overwriting?
                    headers_ordered.append((k,v))
                    # If headers_unset contains same, remove?
                    if k.lower() in headers_unset:
                        headers_unset.remove(k.lower())
            continue
        if it.endswith(";") and find_unescaped(it,";")==len(it)-1:
            k=unescape(it[:-1])
            headers_empty.add(k.lower())
            headers_ordered.append((k,""))
            if k.lower() in headers_unset:
                headers_unset.remove(k.lower())
            continue
        # If we reach here, invalid
        error_exit(f"error: Invalid value for '[REQUEST_ITEM]...': \"{it}\"\n\nUsage: {PROG} [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)

    # After loop, check raw mixing
    if opts.raw is not None and has_data:
        error_exit(f"error: Request body (from --raw) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed.\n\nUsage: xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", code=2)
    # Note: body_file already handled
    return method, parsed, url_full, query_params, json_data, file_fields, headers_ordered, headers_unset, headers_empty, body_file, has_data
